title: The southern map
hookLine: India to Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Java

cards: Put your finger on the plain of the Ganges, where the Buddha walked and taught. Slide it south, down the long coast of India, across a narrow strait to the island of Sri Lanka.
Swing east across the Bay of Bengal to Myanmar. Keep going into Thailand, up the river to Laos, down into Cambodia, and out across the sea to the island of Java.
For weeks this path has walked that line one place at a time. Today, the whole southern map at once.

teach.b: First stop, India, where it began: councils of monks gathering to keep the teaching straight, and an emperor, Ashoka, sending messengers outward. Second, Sri Lanka.

teach.h: SRI LANKA: MAHINDA AND THE TREE.
teach.b: The island's chronicles say Ashoka's son, the monk Mahinda, brought the teaching there, and a cutting of the Bodhi tree followed. The island became a keeper of the Pali texts.
Third, the mainland: Myanmar, Thailand, Laos and Cambodia.

Here the teaching traveled with monks, with traders, and with kings who built and gave. You've met Sukhothai's walking Buddhas, the smiling towers of Angkor, and the saffron line at dawn in Luang Prabang.
Fourth, the sea road to Java, where Borobudur rose as a mountain of carved stone. Now notice what the map doesn't show. A line on a map looks like one clean journey.
It wasn't. The teaching moved back and forth, over a long time. Monks from the mainland sailed to Sri Lanka to be ordained again, and carried the lineage home.
Kings sent for texts and teachers. Some places took up other forms of Buddhism, and some, like Java, later took up other faiths.
Today the Theravada tradition, the way of the elders, lives on in Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos and Cambodia, and its monks chant the same Pali texts.
A monk in Colombo and a monk in Vientiane can recite the same verses in the same old language.
That shared voice is the southern road.

how: Theravada monks in Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia chant the Pali texts daily, and monks from these countries have long visited and ordained in one another's monasteries.

o: nowhere: you start a new lineage yourself.
across the sea to Sri Lanka, to be ordained again.

practice: If you have a map or a phone nearby, find India, then Sri Lanka, and follow the coast east; if not, draw the route in the air with one finger, slowly.
Then let the hand rest, and with each breath name one stop: India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Java. At the end, start again.

wordCard.voice: Theravada. The way of the elders, living on in Sri Lanka and across Southeast Asia, chanting the same Pali texts.

orig.note: Pali: theravāda, the way of the elders, the form of Buddhism that lives on along the southern road.

carryVoice: Your line: the southern road. One old language, chanted on many shores. See you tomorrow.
